clips.title: The story
paras: In the pirate haven of Booty Bay, Whiskey Slim finds himself in dire trouble with his captain. During a violent storm off the coast of the Hinterlands, Slim tapped into a seized crate of Pupellyverbos Port, only to lose the bottles to the churning sea. To escape a brutal flogging, he needs an adventurer to retrieve his misplaced grog.

Whiskey Slim's crew was battling severe weather off the Overlook Cliffs, with the shore of the Hinterlands looming nearby, when the sailor sought a dose of liquid courage. His ship had seized a crate of Pupellyverbos Port from a privateer vessel sailing toward Stormwind. Facing waves that threatened to swallow their ship whole, Slim broke into the captain's crate, but a sudden surge swept the bottles right over the side.

Back in Booty Bay, the clock is ticking down as the ship prepares to weigh anchor. Slim dreads facing the cat-o'-nine-tails once his commanding officer realizes the confiscated port is missing. He seeks someone willing to bring back twelve bottles before his theft comes to light.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: We was splicin' the mainbrace somethin' fierce off of the Overlook Cliffs, ol' Hinterlands just in the distance. Thought the seas was goin' to swallow us whole.
Ol' Slim knows all about liquid courage! Cap'n had a crate of Pupellyverbos Port we commandeered from a privateer en route to Stormwind.

So when that storm off of Hinterlands hit, I busted into the grog. Big wave hit and tossed them bottles overboard. Cap'n is goin' to give me a taste o' the cat if ye don't help me get 'em back though!

clips.title: Progress
paras: Sink me! I'm almost outta booze here! Cap'n is goin' to weigh anchor and Ol' Slim will be caught dry as the Tanaris Desert. And once he discovers his port is missing... Blimey!

clips.title: Completion
paras: Shiver me timbers! Ye found the Cap'n's grog!
I owe ye big time, friend.
Seems like a storm is a brewin' outside. Maybe I'll just keep warm with one o' these here bottles while we wait for it to pass....
